payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery designed to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. Independent testing corrected the prototype’s cycle-life claim to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold, retracting the earlier 12,000 figure as improperly normalized. The chemistry achieved 148 Wh/kg gravimetric energy density, has a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale, and must suspend cycling below its 4 °C operating-temperature floor.
